summary: Google DeepMind published a Nature paper describing WeatherNext Cyclones, an AI model that improves cyclone track, intensity and wind-structure forecasts by roughly a day of lead time, and is open-sourcing the model weights and code (WeatherNext 2 and WeatherNext Cyclones) along with a smaller WeatherNext 2-mini variant runnable on a single TPU.

mechanisms.reason: The model achieves state-of-the-art cyclone forecasts using far coarser (cheaper) input resolution than prior specialized models, reducing computational requirements for a comparable or better output.
mechanisms.quote: WeatherNext Cyclones only needs data with a resolution of 28x28km, 100x coarser than traditional models.

practices.reason: Weights and code are released for a state-of-the-art cyclone forecasting model, enabling teams to self-host, fine-tune or build specialized derivatives.
practices.quote: Alongside our Nature paper, we are open sourcing the code and model weights, making them freely available for anyone to build on.

practices.reason: The paper describes a benchmarking methodology against historical cyclones and rival models, which is domain-specific but illustrates a transferable evaluation approach.
practices.quote: We evaluated WeatherNext Cyclones on historical cyclones from 2023 to 2024, benchmarking its deterministic and probabilistic performance against other top weather models.

practices.reason: The stated ability to generate a full 15-day ensemble forecast in under a minute on a single TPU is a serving-efficiency claim, though no reproducible recipe is given.
practices.quote: We can now generate a single 15-day forecast in less than a minute on a TPU, empowering forecasters to quickly evaluate the probability distribution of potentially devastating tail-risks.
